title: Integrate & tune FlashAttention kernels (v2/v3) and investigate transient regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Integrate FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels as selectable execution paths in the runtime kernel selector. Tune heuristics (sequence-length thresholds, batch cutoffs, memory allocation strategy) and investigate a transient regression observed in canary runs where v3 showed increased tail latency and OOMs for some long-prefill workloads. Goals: (1) make FlashAttention v2/v3 available behind feature flags, (2) create robust kernel selection rules that avoid regressions across GPU families, and (3) add CI perf gates to prevent reintroduction of these regressions.
background: We prototyped FlashAttention v3 for latency wins at medium sequence lengths during last quarter. Early internal benchmarks on A100 (40GB) showed 15-30% token throughput improvement for seq<=2048. During a canary fleet test (canary-2025-02-07) a subset of requests with large prefill + concurrent decode triggered OOMs and increased p95 latency on H100 machines. Investigation points to fragmentation and different workspace allocation behavior in the v3 kernel under heavy KV-cache retention and interleaved prefill/decode scheduling.
observed_regressions: OOMs at seq 4096 when prefill and 4 concurrent decodes run on H100-80GB with batch size 2
p95 token latency increased by ~20% on v3 compared to v2 for mixed prefill/decode workloads (seq 1024-4096)
higher memory fragmentation and increased peak RSS during long prefill windows
root_cause_hypothesis: v3 allocates larger contiguous workspaces; under our allocator it leads to fragmentation when many KV caches coexist
kernel heuristics assume different alignment/stride on SM architectures which results in suboptimal tiling for some model dims
prefill/decode scheduling allows multiple large workspaces to be live concurrently; without micro-batching alignment the peaks overlap
mitigations_implemented: Feature-flagged 'use_flash_v3' behind runtime flag; default keep v2 for now
Added safe fallback in kernel selector: if free_memory < threshold for requested seq on a GPU family, force v2 or generic kernel
Introduced micro-batching threshold for prefill: split prefill into max N chunks when seq>2048 to reduce peak workspace
Adjusted allocator to prefer "small-chunk" pools when KV cache count > 4 (configurable via RUNTIME_FLASH_POOL_SIZE)
Canary rollout paused and resumed behind explicit opt-in for teams running long-prefill workloads
benchmark_plan: Run automated perf matrix nightly across GPUs: A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100, RTX6000; models: llama-2-13b, vicuna-13b; seqs: 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192
Measure: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 token latency, peak RSS, OOM counts (per 100k requests)
Add targeted stress test for prefill+concurrent-decode pattern (prefill seq 4096 + 4 decodes) to CI perf pipeline
Compare Flash v2, Flash v3, and generic aten kernels under identical scheduling policies
acceptance_criteria: No OOMs in nightly matrix for seq<=4096 on supported GPU SKUs (A100/H100) for 7 consecutive runs
p95 with v3 + tuned heuristics <= p95 with v2 for at least 90% of workload slices in benchmark matrix
Kernel selector unit tests covering memory threshold and GPU compute capability branches added and passing
Canary rollout steps documented and rollback tested (runbook + automated flag toggle)
implementation_notes: We will add a kernel-selection YAML mapping keyed by (gpu_family, gpu_mem_gb, model_arch, seq_bucket) that maps to a preferred kernel and fallback list. Use runtime telemetry to collect per-route kernel decisions and annotate traces so data-driven tuning is possible. Avoid changing allocator globally; make pool-size config per node-type and gated behind feature flag.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Defaulting to v2 reduces near-term perf upside for many customers but avoids high-impact OOM regressions
More conservative micro-batching increases latency for some low-concurrency requests — need to tune per-route
Adding more runtime knobs increases operational complexity and burden on SREs

2025-02-18: Allocator tuning PR submitted for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1789 (adds small-chunk pool and config)
2025-02-20: Nightly benchmark matrix added to CI and dashboard created: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/flash-kernel/flash-kernel-matrix
2025-02-24: UX: Added console toggle for 'FlashAttention v3' under performance flags for Dedicated and Private customers (PM review by Sofia Martinez)
2025-02-28: After allocator changes, canary run for 3 days with sequence 4096 saw zero OOMs; preparing rollout plan (Marco Chen)
next_steps: Finalize kernel-selection mapping and promote to staging with canary=10% on runtime-1.20 cluster
Merge allocator PR and land perf CI gates (blocking: ENG-4689 for CI infra updates)
Run one-week soak on mixed customer-like traffic for seq up to 8192 and validate dashboards
Document runbook for rollback and add automated toggle for 'use_flash_v3' feature flag
notes: Experimentally, v3 shows largest wins at seq 1024-2048 on A100; beyond 4096 the memory characteristics dominate. The final selector will prefer v3 for 'short-to-medium' buckets on A100 and keep v2/generic for long sequences unless node has >80GB and allocator pool configured. We'll monitor telemetry for 2 weeks post-release.
